question: Why did the optimization of the hydroquinone-catechol vacuum distillation raise the distillate-to-feed ratio above the industrial baseline?
expect: premise false: D/F was REDUCED from 0.121 to 0.092 (abstract)
rendered:
Document "Rigorous Modeling and Industrial-Scalable Optimization of Hydroquinone-Catechol Vacuum Distillation: Aspen Plus-RSM Integration for Thermally Labile Systems" is the most relevant to the question.

The optimization of the hydroquinone-catechol vacuum distillation process led to a higher distillate-to-feed (D/F) ratio of 0.092, which was initially estimated to ensure effective enrichment of catechol in the distillate while maintaining high-purity hydroquinone in the bottoms. The authors state that this D/F ratio was set as an initial baseline value for the simulation and was treated as an adjustable variable alongside reflux ratio and operating pressure in subsequent optimization via Response Surface Methodology (RSM).
